# nemau_load_balancer (Resource)

A load balancer. Its VIP is allocated in `vip_subnet_id`; `flavor` picks the tier, and the high-availability tiers run two appliances on two hosts behind that VIP.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nemau_load_balancer" "edge" {
  name          = "edge"
  vip_subnet_id = nemau_subnet.app.id
  flavor        = "lb-ha"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Load balancer name. Changes in place.
- `vip_subnet_id` (String) Id of the subnet the VIP is allocated in. Changing it replaces the load balancer.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-form description. Changes in place.
- `flavor` (String) The tier: `lb-small` (one appliance, the default), or `lb-ha`, `lb-medium`, `lb-large` (two appliances on two hosts, active and standby behind the VIP). The platform does not change a tier in place, so changing it replaces the load balancer and allocates a new VIP.

### Read-Only

- `appliance_addresses` (List of String) The addresses health checks and proxied connections leave from: the VIP on `lb-small`, each appliance's own address on a high-availability tier. The members' security groups must admit them.
- `id` (String) Load balancer id.
- `operating_status` (String) Operating status as reported by the platform.
- `provider_engine` (String) The engine the load balancer runs. It is read-only. A new load balancer is always `auto`, which accepts `HTTP`, `HTTPS`, `TCP` and `UDP` listeners side by side; an older load balancer may report `haproxy` (no `UDP` listeners) or `nginx` (`UDP` listeners only). The attribute is named `provider_engine` because `provider` is reserved in Terraform.
- `provisioning_status` (String) Provisioning status as reported by the platform.
- `vip_address` (String) The VIP: the address clients connect to, taken from `vip_subnet_id`.

## Import

```shell
# A load balancer imports by its id.
terraform import nemau_load_balancer.edge 1f6c3a8e-4b9d-4e27-9a53-8d2e5b0c7f19
```
